name: MathlibAnnex.EquivalentSeminorm
title: A seminorm with two-sided bounds against a reference norm

content.display_title: A seminorm with two-sided bounds against a reference norm
content.one_sentence_role: Records a norm through a seminorm, two positive comparison constants and continuity on the original normed space.
content.natural_language_statement:
Let $X$ be a real normed space with reference norm $\|\cdot\|$. An equivalent-seminorm datum consists of a real seminorm $p$ and constants $c,C>0$ such that

$$c\|x\|\le p(x)\le C\|x\|\qquad(x\in X),$$

together with continuity of $p$ for the reference topology. The record keeps this comparison data explicit.
content.definition_explanation: The eight fields are: (1) the seminorm $p$; (2) a real lower constant $c$; (3) a real upper constant $C$; (4) a proof that $c>0$; (5) a proof that $C>0$; (6) the lower comparison $c\|x\|\le p(x)$ for every $x$; (7) the upper comparison $p(x)\le C\|x\|$ for every $x$; and (8) continuity of $p$. These fields specify data and its properties; constructing such a record requires supplying all eight.
content.assumptions: The carrier $X$ is a real normed vector space. The stored function $p:X\to\mathbb R$ is a seminorm: it is subadditive, nonnegative and satisfies $p(tx)=|t|p(x)$. Both comparison constants are strictly positive, both inequalities hold for every $x$, and continuity of $p$ is part of the stored data. There is no finite-dimensionality or completeness assumption.
content.conclusion: The lower bound makes $p$ definite: if $p(x)=0$, then $0\le c\|x\|\le0$; since $c>0$, $\|x\|=0$ and $x=0$. This is the separately proved definiteness lemma. The related definitions give $B_p=\{x:p(x)\le1\}$ and $S_p=\{x:p(x)=1\}$. In particular $B_p\subseteq\{x:\|x\|\le1/c\}$, by the bounded-ball lemma.
content.lean_realization_notes: The reference norm on $X$ remains in place. The separate construction $\mathrm{Space}(p)$ equips a copy of the carrier with norm $p$; its distance is $p(x-y)$, as recorded in the cited transport theorem. Boundedness of $B_p$ alone does not assert compactness in an arbitrary infinite-dimensional space.
